thread:
maya: Heads-up — saw a perf regression on the 0a1b2c3 runtime change. Latency p50 for long contexts jumped ~2x on A100. Started profiling with nsys and nvprof.

sam: ugh. which workload and sequence len?

maya: seq_len=2048, batch=1 (streaming chat). Before/after runs attached below. nsys timeline shows more time in cublasLtMatmul compared to our fused attention kernel.

ryan: can you paste the nsys summary?

maya: nvprof summary (post-change):
```
GPU activities:
  1.  cublasLtMatmul                  Time(%)  42.7    Calls  38   Avg  12.4ms  
  2.  custom_fused_attn_kernel        Time(%)  18.1    Calls  38   Avg   5.3ms
  3.  softmax                         Time(%)  8.0     Calls  76   Avg   2.1ms
  4.  memcpy H2D                      Time(%)  3.2
```

maya: pre-change (master@before):
```
GPU activities:
  1.  custom_fused_attn_kernel        Time(%)  48.5    Calls  38   Avg  10.3ms
  2.  cublasLtMatmul                  Time(%)  12.2    Calls  38   Avg   2.6ms
  3.  softmax                         Time(%)  9.1
```

sam: wow that's a clear shift. kernel selector must be preferring cublasLt now. did you run with env OVERRIDE_KERNEL?

maya: yes — I forced KERNEL_SELECTOR=force_fused and latency returned to baseline. Means behavioral change in selector or profiling heuristics elsewhere.

ryan: any code changes in selector around that commit?

maya: git show 0a1b2c3 --name-only
```
M	runtime/kernel_selector.cc
M	runtime/profiling/heuristics.cc
M	tests/profiler_integration.cc
```

maya: I did a quick git-bisect:
```
git bisect start bad good
# ran profile script that nsys profiles and checks median p50
git bisect run ./tools/ci/profile-bisect.sh
```

maya: bisect landed on 0a1b2c3 — change in heuristics.cc replaced our microbenchmark-based scoring with a simplified cost-per-token model that seems to favor matmul primitives for certain dims.

sam: can you attach perfetto timeline snippets (before/after)? those help for concurrency view.

maya: uploaded links (perfetto): https://perfetto.dev/trace/viewer?trace=pre-change-blob and https://perfetto.dev/trace/viewer?trace=post-change-blob (internal redwood storage). Post-change shows bigger gaps between kernel launches and higher cublas occupancy.

ryan: is this reproducible on other hw (V100 or T4)?

maya: reproduced on V100 with similar relative regression (1.6x). T4 shows smaller delta (1.2x), likely due to microkernel perf curve.

sam: guess: the new heuristic computes score = flop_est / measured_bandwidth and picks cublas when score < threshold. But our fused kernel benefits from better memory reuse; the estimator undercounts reuse.

maya: exactly. heuristic uses naive flop estimates ignoring KV-cache locality for prefix caching. If prefix kv hit-rate is high, fused path much faster. 0a1b2c removed kv-aware term.

ryan: quick mitigation: add a short-circuit in selector: if kv_cache_hit_ratio > 0.3 and seq_len>512, prefer fused. Should be safe until we rework estimator.

maya: implemented quick patch and ran nsys: p50 back to baseline. opened PR #4892 with test and perf traces attached.

sam: nice. add a unit perf test to CI (profile-bisect.sh) that asserts <1.2x regression vs golden.

ci-bot: CI perf sample registered: build/4892/profile-test queued (:hourglass:).

ops-bot: deploy note — don't roll this to Dedicated pools until perf PR is merged and smoke-tested.

maya: agreed. follow-up items I added to the PR:
- reintroduce kv-aware term into estimator (long-term)
- add microbenchmarks for different seq_len/batch combos to cost DB
- add bisect harness to nightly perf job to catch selector regressions

ryan: also add an entry to release notes: "selector: fixed heuristic causing cublas preference for long-contexts".

sam: thanks maya — can you drop the nsys timeline PNGs in the PR? I'll review the code tomorrow. :thumbsup:

maya: done. thanks all.

(attachment: nsys_post.png, nsys_pre.png, perfetto_post.trace, perfetto_pre.trace)
